verdicts.reasoning: An act of identification is what the clause isolates, and three seeds require it: two ask which of four named shapes has NO line of symmetry (key: a scalene triangle), and one asks whether a heart split down the middle shows line symmetry. In each the learner must sort symmetric cases from non-symmetric ones rather than recall a fact, so the identifying behaviour is present even though the candidates arrive as words.

verdicts.reasoning: Not one sample in this block carries a VISUAL RENDERED line, so there is no drawn shape or figure anywhere in the evidence. A learner meeting 'a scalene triangle' as three words has to recall its properties from memory; they cannot inspect a figure, which is what a shapes-or-figures clause requires of the presentation.
